strengths: No stock “Japan is a country where / unique aspect / it may seem strange” scaffolding.
Magazine cadence: short scenes, then a toolkit thesis, then named practices.
Phrases like “mild tax,” “re-enter the group,” and “receipt for care” sound like an editor, not a brochure.
Closing stays specific (scale, home entry, no arms race) instead of “this fascinating custom.”

issues.problem: Snarky metaphor; slightly AI-clever and off the calm magazine voice.
issues.suggestion: Replace with “not absorbed by osmosis” or “not something everyone just knows.”

issues.location: Why Gifts Do Social Work — “Interpretation:” label
issues.problem: Reads like an editorial pipeline stamp rather than a sentence.
issues.suggestion: Fold into prose: “Frequency comes from stacked calendars—trips, visits, ceremonies—not a national hobby.”

issues.location: Households as stages — “spiritually if not legally”
issues.problem: Winking legalese; a bit cute for the point (empty-handed visits exist elsewhere).
issues.suggestion: “Related to, not unique to Japan: don’t arrive empty-handed. The local version is more standardized in form.”

issues.location: How Japanese People Experience the Small Bag — “The cookies are not about the cookies.”
issues.problem: Aphorism works once; it rhymes with the closing “the point was never the object,” which doubles the slogan.
issues.suggestion: Keep one; let the office-reentry sentence carry the other.
